meta.note: Only people and organisations that actually operationalised AGI: a stated criterion concrete enough to check. Definitions with no threshold or measurement procedure are excluded. Entries marked claim=proxy are widely read as AGI progress indicators but were never framed as AGI tests by their authors; they are listed separately on the page.

definitions.name: The Turing Test
definitions.progress_note: 73% judged human against a 50% three-party bar
definitions.quote: an average interrogator will not have more than 70 per cent chance of making the right identification after five minutes of questioning
definitions.status_today: Passed in 2025, against a bar Turing never set. His 70% figure was a prediction for the year 2000 and describes interrogator accuracy, not the pass mark used here. The bar actually cleared is the 50% chance line in a three-party test. Jones and Bergen ran two randomised, pre-registered three-party tests, on UC San Diego undergraduates and an online Prolific sample: five-minute simultaneous conversations with one human and one system, then a judgement of which was which. GPT-4.5 with a humanlike-persona prompt was judged to be the human 73% of the time, significantly more often than the actual human participants. LLaMa-3.1-405B also cleared the bar at 56%, so two systems passed, not one. Two caveats keep this honest: without the persona prompt the same model drops to 36%, and the systems that passed are generations behind the frontier. Published in PNAS in May 2026.
definitions.verification_note: Peer-reviewed PNAS study, pre-registered, no lab involvement
definitions.flip_condition: A failed replication at longer duration, or without a persona prompt, would reopen this.

definitions.name: The Coffee Test
definitions.quote: a machine to enter an average American home and figure out how to make coffee
definitions.quote_source: Steve Wozniak. Find the machine, the coffee, a mug and water, and operate an unfamiliar appliance, in a house it has never seen
definitions.status_today: Not passed, and never attempted. No robot has entered an unfamiliar home, found the kitchen, the coffee and a mug, and worked out an appliance it had never seen. The best independent evidence is Epoch AI's February 2026 task-by-task audit, which rates "clean a kitchen" at tier 2 of 5, significant limits in lab, and "cook simple meals" at tier 1, early research stage. The clause this test turns on is appliance transfer: handed an unfamiliar appliance and a zero-shot instruction, Physical Intelligence's π0.7 makes a reasonable attempt and does not finish, and succeeds only with step-by-step human coaching. Navigation and object search in homes absent from training are genuinely demonstrated, so this is well short of zero. Kitchen demonstrations from Figure, 1X and Physical Intelligence are real but instrumented, trained, or in 1X's case substantially teleoperated. Nobody has done it cold in a stranger's house. Forecasters surveyed in April 2026 put the median pass at 2034.
definitions.verification_note: Never attempted in an unfamiliar home; scored as a judgement over Epoch AI's component-level assessments
definitions.flip_condition: One unrehearsed run in a home the system has never seen, operating an unfamiliar appliance unaided.
definitions.progress_note: component progress against a test never run

definitions.name: 85% on ARC-AGI-2
definitions.quote: Can you create a system that can reach 85% accuracy?
definitions.quote_source: ARC Prize Foundation, 2025. The prize is scored on the private set, inside a compute-limited offline container.
definitions.status_today: ARC-AGI-2 has two scores and the gap between them is the whole story. On the semi-private set, which frontier API models are evaluated against, GPT-5.6 Sol reaches 92.5% and Claude Opus 5 reaches 90.4%. Six configurations now clear the 85% bar, at $0.74 to $2.06 per task. Inside the compute-limited offline container the prize actually uses, the last adjudicated result is 24%, set by team NVARC in the 2025 competition. The 2026 private leaderboard does not exist until submissions close on 2 November, with results on 4 December, so nothing in-container is final before then. The per-task costs above describe API runs and are not comparable to the Kaggle track's cost regime. One correction to how this prize is usually described: the 85% threshold unlocks a $150,000 Bonus Prize, which rolls forward to 2027 if unmet. The $275,000 Grand Prize goes to the best solution writeup, and $700,000 is the whole track pool.
definitions.verification_note: Adjudicated inside ARC Prize's own Kaggle competition
definitions.claim_note: Chollet has said plainly that solving ARC-AGI would not mean AGI had been achieved. The prize is framed as a necessary milestone, not a finish line.
definitions.flip_condition: The 4 December 2026 private-set result. 85% claims the $150K bonus; below that it rolls to 2027.

definitions.name: ARC-AGI-3: interactive novel environments
definitions.quote: An interactive reasoning benchmark which challenges AI agents to explore novel environments, acquire goals on the fly, build adaptable world models, and learn continuously.
definitions.quote_source: ARC Prize Foundation, launched 25 March 2026. A 100% score means agents beat every environment as efficiently as humans.
definitions.status_today: 30.16% against a human 100%. Agents get no instructions, no rules and no stated goals. They must explore, infer how the environment works, work out what winning looks like, and carry what they learn forward. At launch in March 2026 the best frontier model scored 0.51%. Claude Opus 5, tested on 24 July, scored 30.16%, roughly four times the next best system, GPT-5.6 Sol at 7.8%, with every older frontier model still near zero. That is the largest single-step gain on any AGI-framed benchmark right now, and it is one vendor's unreplicated result. On cost the picture is less one-sided than it looks: the run came to $20,657, which is nowhere near human on the efficiency dimension Chollet's definition cares about, but it undercut the $25,064 GPT-5.6 Sol spent to score 7.8%. Both figures are from the published semi-private leaderboard.
definitions.verification_note: ARC Prize tested Claude Opus 5 directly, but the result is one vendor's, unreplicated
definitions.claim_note: AGI-framed by name, but the ARC Prize Foundation claims it as a measure of one missing capability, not as a sufficient test for general intelligence.
definitions.flip_condition: An independent replication of the 30.16%, or any system clearing it at materially lower cost.

definitions.name: The AGI Score: ten cognitive domains
definitions.affiliation: CAIS, with Bengio, Marcus, Schmidt, Tegmark and ~28 others
definitions.quote: AGI is an AI that can match or exceed the cognitive versatility and proficiency of a well-educated adult.
definitions.quote_source: "A Definition of AGI", October 2025. Grounded in Cattell-Horn-Carroll theory, the most empirically validated model of human cognition
definitions.status_today: Ten cognitive domains, each weighted 10%, scored with adapted human psychometric batteries. GPT-4 scored 27%. GPT-5 scored 57%. The single most striking result is that both score 0% on Long-Term Memory Storage. They cannot permanently learn anything after deployment. Because domains are weighted equally, that one zero caps any current-architecture system at 90%, which makes this the strongest available argument that scaling alone cannot finish the job. Two caveats: equal weighting is a value judgement with no empirical backing, and the score is stale. No 2026 model has been run through this framework, so the most-cited number in AGI discourse is nine months and several model generations old.
definitions.verification_note: Scored by the paper's own authors and never independently replicated; no 2026 model has been run at all
definitions.flip_condition: Any 2026 frontier model scored on the ten domains. A non-zero Long-Term Memory Storage score would be the bigger event.

definitions.name: The Hutter Prize: compression as intelligence
definitions.progress_note: under 6% of the purse paid; a money metric, not a byte one
definitions.quote: enwik9 constitutes an amount of non-visual knowledge an average adult human holds, so compressors compressing enwik9 better than a human will predict better, and hence should be smarter... which, if achieved, most would agree constitutes AGI.
definitions.status_today: Twenty years old, still running, and the numbers are sobering. The official record is 110,793,128 bytes, set in September 2024, and under 6% of the €500,000 pool has ever been paid out. A June 2026 entry that would clear the next 1% bar was still unawarded at the time of review. The best unconstrained compressor in the world is a transformer, nncp v3.2 at 106.6 MB, comfortably better than the record. It cannot win, because it violates the prize's rules limiting entrants to 50 hours on a single CPU core with 10GB of RAM. The prize was designed on the premise that compression is intelligence; when neural methods started winning at compression, the resource constraints kept them out.
definitions.verification_note: Prize committee adjudicates every award against a byte count
definitions.flip_condition: An award to the pending cmix-lex entry, or a rule change admitting neural compressors.

definitions.name: $100B in cumulative profits
definitions.progress_note: cumulative losses, not profits; clause deleted before it could resolve
definitions.quote: systems that have the ability to generate the maximum total profits to which its earliest investors, including Microsoft, are entitled
definitions.quote_source: Reported by The Information, Dec 2024. The contract itself is not public
definitions.status_today: This definition no longer exists. The AGI clause was removed from the Microsoft–OpenAI agreement on 27 April 2026; Microsoft's announcement of the amended deal does not contain the word AGI at all. No AGI was ever declared, so the expert panel created to verify such a declaration never had anything to verify. The clause is void, but the metric it named is still measurable, and the answer is that progress runs away from the threshold. Financial statements obtained by Ed Zitron and the Financial Times in June 2026 show OpenAI on $13.07B of 2025 revenue against a $20.92B operating loss, after $3.7B and $8.78B respectively in 2024. Cumulative profits since inception are deeply negative, so reaching $100B cumulative would require well over $130B of future profit from a company that has told investors it does not expect positive cash flow until around 2030. Three things are near-universally misreported here: the clause specified profits, not revenue; the figure was cumulative, not annual; and it was pegged to the capped-profit structure OpenAI itself dissolved in October 2025. It was settled by renegotiation, not by anyone crossing a technical line.
definitions.verification_note: Rests on the two counterparties' own disclosures; the contract has never been public
definitions.flip_condition: Nothing. The clause was deleted; only the underlying profit figure can still move.

definitions.name: Expert parity on real occupational deliverables
definitions.quote: a domain expert sees only the task and two unlabeled deliverables, and ranks them without knowing which is which
definitions.quote_source: GDPval grading protocol, as described by Epoch AI, 2026
definitions.status_today: 1,320 tasks across 44 occupations, drawn from real deliverables by professionals averaging 14 years' experience, graded by blind pairwise comparison against a human expert's work. Parity has been reached on the benchmark's own metric. The paper reports wins-or-ties, putting Claude Opus 4.1 at 47.6%; GPT-5.2 reached 70.9% and GPT-5.5 later 84.9%. Quote these like for like: GPT-5.2's straight win rate is 49.7%, against 21.2% ties and 29.1% losses, so it is graded better than the expert more than twice as often as worse. Epoch AI's reading is that GPT-5.2 reached parity. Epoch's February 2026 verdict is the part that matters. GDPval "is falling short in its role as a leading indicator for automation." It was built to predict economic impact, it reached parity, and the impact has not followed.
definitions.verification_note: Scored by Epoch AI and Artificial Analysis, though the benchmark is OpenAI's own
definitions.claim_note: OpenAI built GDPval to measure economic task performance and never claimed parity on it constitutes AGI. Reading it as an AGI threshold is this page's inference, not OpenAI's claim.
definitions.flip_condition: A GDPval-style result tracking a measurable labour-market shift, which Epoch says has not happened.

definitions.name: The world economy growing at 10%
definitions.quote: Us self-claiming some AGI milestone, that's just nonsensical benchmark hacking to me. The real benchmark is: the world growing at 10%.
definitions.status_today: Nobody has to convene a panel to score this one: the IMF publishes it quarterly and has no stake in the AGI debate. It is also the only criterion here that starts from a floor rather than from zero. The world economy grows at roughly 3% a year without any AI contribution at all — 3.2% averaged across 1970 to 2019, 3.0% across the 2009-2019 decade. The IMF's July 2026 update projects 3.0% for 2026, revised down again from the 3.1% it published in April. Measured as excess over the no-AI baseline, which is the only way this criterion means anything, progress toward Nadella's 10% is zero, and the sign is negative. What growth there is looks like the economy building the factory rather than the factory producing. Summing the national-accounts lines for information-processing equipment and intellectual property puts roughly three-quarters of Q1 2026 US growth in that bucket, though the BEA publishes no AI-specific line. Goldman Sachs reports finding no meaningful economy-wide relationship between AI adoption and productivity. The criterion cannot attribute growth to any particular cause, but it is immune to benchmark gaming, which was Nadella's point.

evidence.label: Epoch: AI datacenter share of GDP

definitions.flip_condition: Global growth sustained above roughly 4%, which would be the first clear excess over the long-run baseline. Two consecutive IMF outlooks above 5% would put the bar in reach.

definitions.name: Turn $100,000 into $1,000,000
definitions.affiliation: CEO, Microsoft AI; co-founder of DeepMind
definitions.quote: Go make $1 million on a retail web platform in a few months with just a $100,000 investment.
definitions.quote_source: Mustafa Suleyman, MIT Technology Review, July 2023
definitions.status_today: Not passed, and the balance is moving the wrong way. The criterion is unusually checkable: a stake, a multiple, a venue, a deadline, and a bank balance as the scorekeeper. Since 10 April 2026 Andon Labs has run the nearest thing to a real attempt: an AI agent given a San Francisco storefront and a starting stake reported at $100,000, operating the business end to end. As of 27 July the bank balance stands at $62,719, and over the trailing month the store took $2,852 in revenue against $3,444 in token costs. Andon's own write-up states plainly that the store is not profitable. In simulation the picture is better and still short: the best model on Vending-Bench 2 reaches roughly 17% of a skilled human's estimated $63,000 over a simulated year. The test is usually shortened to "turn $100K into $1M", but the original specifies on a retail web platform, which rules out the trading and crypto strategies most likely to produce a spurious pass.
definitions.verification_note: Attempted with real money since April 2026, but the figures are the operator's own and not independently audited
definitions.flip_condition: Any audited AI-run business turning $100k into $1M on a retail web platform. Andon Market returning to its starting balance would be the leading indicator.
definitions.progress_note: real-money attempt running at a loss

definitions.name: Powerful AI: a country of geniuses in a datacenter
definitions.quote: It does not just passively answer questions; instead, it can be given tasks that take hours, days, or weeks to complete, and then goes off and does those tasks autonomously, in the way a smart employee would.
definitions.quote_source: Dario Amodei, "Machines of Loving Grace", October 2024
definitions.status_today: Amodei rejects the term AGI and defines "powerful AI" by the five properties listed above. Two are comfortably met. Two are partial. One cannot be tested at all, and it is the one carrying the definition: nobody has proposed a way to check whether a system is "smarter than a Nobel Prize winner across most relevant fields." The autonomy clause is where the action is, because METR measures it directly. The last published frontier figure is 17.4 hours at 50% reliability, and about 3.1 hours at 80%. Hours, yes. Days, marginally. Weeks, no. The score is an unweighted mean across the five properties, which flatters the result, because Amodei states them as a conjunction where every one must hold. His 2024 essay put powerful AI "as early as 2026"; the January 2026 restatement moved that to one or two years without noting the earlier window had expired.

criteria.label: Smarter than a Nobel Prize winner across most relevant fields
criteria.note: No test, no threshold, no evaluator. This is the property the whole definition rests on and the only one he never operationalized.

criteria.label: All the interfaces of a human working virtually: text, audio, video, mouse and keyboard, internet
criteria.note: Shipped across frontier models; computer-use agents are in production.

criteria.label: Runs tasks taking hours, days or weeks autonomously
criteria.note: METR's frontier 50% horizon is 17.4h, but METR calls measurements above 16h unreliable with its current suite (95% CI 8.5-55h) and excludes the point from its own trend fit. It is also a preview snapshot, not a shipped model.

criteria.label: Controls physical tools, robots and lab equipment through a computer
criteria.note: Real in instrumented settings. Epoch AI rates the nearest household task at tier 2 of 5, and transfer to unseen environments is largely undemonstrated.

criteria.label: Millions of parallel instances at 10-100x human speed
criteria.note: Not in doubt. GDPval measured frontier models completing expert deliverables around 100x faster.

definitions.flip_condition: A published method for testing the Nobel-laureate clause would make the criterion scoreable; METR horizons past a week at 80% reliability would move the autonomy clause.

definitions.name: Automated AI R&D: the three labs' own trigger
definitions.affiliation: written independently, in their safety frameworks
definitions.quote: recursively self improving (i.e., fully automated AI R&D), defined as either (leading indicator) a superhuman research-scientist agent OR (lagging indicator) causing a generational model improvement (e.g., from OpenAI o1 to OpenAI o3) in 1/5th the wall-clock time of equivalent progress in 2024, sustainably for several months
definitions.quote_source: OpenAI Preparedness Framework v2. The Critical threshold for AI Self-Improvement
definitions.status_today: Untriggered at all three labs. Anthropic, OpenAI and Google DeepMind each wrote a recursive-AI-R&D threshold into a safety framework, independently, with every commercial incentive to claim capability. Anthropic's Claude Opus 5 system card of 24 July states the automated AI R&D threshold is not crossed, on the grounds that no sustained AI-attributable 2x acceleration is observed and the model does not substitute for its research staff. OpenAI's card for GPT-5.6 puts all three variants below the High rung for AI self-improvement, the step immediately beneath Critical. All three are rated High for biological, chemical and cyber capability. Gemini 3.1 Pro Deep Think reaches no DeepMind Critical Capability Level. Unlike benchmark scores, these are negative determinations with legal and reputational exposure attached. The obvious caveat: all three are self-assessed, and no regulator publishes an independent determination against these thresholds.
definitions.verification_note: All three determinations are made by the labs about their own models; no regulator publishes an independent finding
definitions.claim_note: These are risk-management triggers written for safety frameworks. None of the three labs says crossing one means AGI has arrived, though all three treat it as the point where progress stops being human-paced.
definitions.flip_condition: Any of the three labs publishing a determination that its own threshold has been crossed.

definitions.name: Three of five tasks, by one system
definitions.affiliation: offered to Elon Musk; criteria co-authored with Ernest Davis
definitions.progress_note: none met, three partial, of five
definitions.quote: if you (or anyone else) manages to beat at least three of them in 2029 — with a single system; three separate systems would obviously not count as general — you win; if only one or two are broken, we can't very well say we have nailed the general part in artificial general intelligence, can we?
definitions.quote_source: Gary Marcus, "Dear Elon Musk", 31 May 2022 (generality clause added June 2024)
definitions.status_today: This is an unaccepted offer, not a bet. No money has ever been at risk. Marcus offered $100,000 in May 2022; within a week Vivek Wadhwa and others had matched it to $500,000. Musk never responded, then or to the $1M and $10M offers that followed. Any description of this as "Marcus's bet with Musk" is wrong. None of the five tasks are unambiguously met by a single system, which is the bar the offer actually sets. The kitchen task is furthest away, and it is the one Marcus himself later excluded from his real wager with Miles Brundage as too dependent on robotics.
definitions.verification_note: Never adjudicated; the offer was never accepted, so no panel exists

criteria.label: Watch a film and say accurately what is going on
criteria.note: VideoOdyssey, on feature-length video: 56.3% for the best model against 84.4% for humans.

criteria.label: Read a novel and answer questions beyond the literal text
criteria.note: NoCha: 68.5% for the best model against 96.9% for humans, and no 2026 frontier model has been run on it.

criteria.label: Work as a competent cook in an arbitrary kitchen
criteria.note: π0.7 does zero-shot multi-stage kitchen-appliance tasks in homes absent from training, but needed roughly 30 minutes of human coaching to work an air fryer. Not a cook. Marcus later excluded this task from his real bet as too hardware-dependent.

criteria.label: Reliably construct bug-free code of more than 10,000 lines from a natural language specification, or by interacting with a non-expert user
criteria.note: No demonstration at this scale. METR's best 80%-reliability time horizon is about three hours. Markets price this task at 80%, behind novel comprehension.

criteria.label: Convert arbitrary proofs from the mathematical literature, written in natural language, into a symbolic form suitable for verification
criteria.note: Whole-paper autoformalisation arrived in 2026: LeanMarathon formalised seven target theorems with no 'sorry' across two research papers. But those were hand-selected, and models still fail to stay faithful when a proof is paraphrased or a value changed.

definitions.flip_condition: A single system doing three of the five. Musk accepting would turn the offer into a bet.

definitions.name: Eight of ten tasks by end of 2027
definitions.affiliation: Brundage: formerly OpenAI Senior Advisor for AGI Readiness
definitions.progress_note: none met, four partial, of ten
definitions.quote: Both of us agree that the achievement of 8 out of 10 of these tasks would be strong evidence for the G (General) in Artificial General Intelligence having been achieved. For the purpose of the bet, the tasks should not be performed by 10 completely separate systems.
definitions.quote_source: Marcus & Brundage, 30 December 2024. Accepted, funded and live
definitions.status_today: This is the real wager, and the one that should be cited instead of the Musk offers. Ten tasks, robotics deliberately excluded, resolving 31 December 2027. None are met. Every task carrying a primary measurement sits well below its bar: films 56.3% against 84.4% for humans on feature-length video, novels 68.5% against 96.9%, mastering an unseen game 30.2% against a human 100%. The maths task is the cleanest arithmetic on this page, because footnote 3 of the bet sets it at twenty papers formalised twenty out of twenty, and the best 2026 system managed two hand-selected papers. Legal briefs carry the strongest real-world disconfirmation anywhere on this site: a database of court decisions on AI-fabricated citations records 1,509 cases involving fabricated material, 703 of them filed by practising lawyers. Marcus is heavily favoured, at 88% on Metaculus. The most informative thing about the bet is a factual dispute nobody has adjudicated: the crowd rationale says "six out of ten tasks likely solved already," while Marcus's own December 2025 audit says "no system solved more than 4 (or maybe any)." Markets put 22.8% on the bet being annulled, because the panel of judges that decides it still does not publicly exist.
definitions.verification_note: The judging panel that decides it has still not been named
definitions.flip_condition: Eight of ten by 31 Dec 2027, or the naming of a judging panel, which would cut the 22.8% annulment price.

definitions.name: A Turing Test passed by 2029
definitions.affiliation: Long Bets #1, the inaugural Long Now wager
definitions.progress_note: protocol at zero, capability at a weaker proxy
definitions.quote: each of the three Turing Test Judges will conduct online interviews of each of the four Turing Test Candidates for two hours each for a total of eight hours of interviews conducted by each of the three Judges (for a total of 24 hours of interviews)
definitions.quote_source: The Kurzweil–Kapor rules, agreed 2002. Requiring both a Human Determination Test and a Rank Order Test
definitions.status_today: Unresolved and never attempted. In twenty-four years no committee has been seated, no interview conducted, and the detailed rules the 2002 agreement promised that committee would write have never been written. The executable half of this criterion sits at zero. The capability half passed a much weaker version. GPT-4.5 was judged human 73% of the time in the PNAS study, but only with a humanlike-persona prompt; without it the same model scored 36%. Those conversations ran five minutes, with a pre-registered fifteen-minute replication. This wager demands two-hour interviews from each of three judges, roughly 24 times longer, plus a rank-order test. Nothing measures that. What forecasters worry about is not capability. Metaculus's question on a long adversarial Turing test lists as its sole key factor: "Big companies unlikely to run Turing test soon." The deepest market on the Long Bets version sits near even odds, well down from its peak, not on capability pessimism but on the expectation that nobody will bother to run it.
definitions.verification_note: No committee seated and no interview conducted in 24 years
definitions.flip_condition: A committee being seated. Nothing else can resolve this before 2029.

definitions.name: The Einstein Test: derive general relativity from 1911
definitions.quote: training an AI system with a knowledge cutoff of, say, 1911, and then seeing if it could come up with general relativity like Einstein did in 1915. That's the kind of true test of whether we have a full AGI system.
definitions.quote_source: Demis Hassabis, India AI Impact Summit, 19 February 2026
definitions.status_today: Not met, by Hassabis's own assessment. He added in the same breath that "it's clear today's systems couldn't do that." The test has been run once, far below frontier scale. In March 2026 Michael Hla trained a 3.3B-parameter model on roughly 22B tokens of pre-1900 text and prompted it with the observations behind relativity and the photoelectric effect. It produced fragments that sound right beside steam-engine nonsense, and his own verdict was pattern-matching rather than physics. A negative result three orders of magnitude below the frontier constrains very little. The corpus objection is weaker than it looks, too: TypewriterLM, released in June 2026, is a 7.24B-parameter model trained on 54B tokens with a 1913 cutoff and explicit leakage mitigation. Bounded corpora are tractable. Nobody has trained at a scale where failure would be informative. The nearest discovery evidence cuts both ways. In May 2026 an internal OpenAI reasoning model disproved the Erdős unit distance conjecture, open since 1946, verified by external mathematicians including Tim Gowers and Noga Alon though not yet through journal peer review. Genuine, but a result inside an existing paradigm, not a theory derived from a deliberately impoverished knowledge base.
definitions.drift: Hassabis is the clearest case of raising the bar while shortening the clock. His long-standing definition was "all the cognitive capabilities humans can", a median-human bar. DeepMind's April 2025 safety paper then anchored planning on "Exceptional AGI" at the 99th percentile; a December 2025 DeepMind podcast made world models and physical understanding prerequisites, which structurally disqualifies text-only models; February 2026 added the Einstein Test. Over the same period his timeline went from 5–10 years to 2–5.
definitions.verification_note: Run once at small scale (3.3B parameters, pre-1900 corpus, March 2026) with a negative result; never attempted at frontier scale
definitions.flip_condition: A frontier-scale run on a pre-1911 corpus. TypewriterLM shows the corpus is buildable; only the scale is missing.

definitions.name: Weakly general AI: four tests, one system
definitions.quote: a single unified software system that can satisfy the following criteria, all easily completable by a typical college-educated human
definitions.quote_source: Metaculus question 3479. The unified clause bars a system "cobbled together as a set of sub-systems specialized to tasks like the above"
definitions.status_today: The live blocker here is sample efficiency, not raw capability, which makes it unlike anything else on this page. Two of the four tests are settled and one is close. The fourth asks for Montezuma's Revenge, all 24 rooms, from visual input alone, learned in under 100 hours of equivalent play. The rooms themselves stopped being the hard part in 2018, when Go-Explore reached level 1 reliably. The budget is the bar: Go-Explore and the exploration methods that followed consumed sample counts far beyond a hundred hours of play. A top-voted comment on the question calls this the only criterion not yet satisfied, and its author puts even odds on it falling by 2030. The unification clause is the second live constraint, and it is the one nobody is trying to satisfy: no single system has been demonstrated doing all four. The community estimate is 13 September 2028, from 1.8k forecasters.
definitions.flip_condition: A single system clearing Montezuma's Revenge inside the sample budget, then demonstrated on the other three tests without retraining.
definitions.verification_note: Never adjudicated as a whole; no system has been tested against all four criteria together

criteria.label: Pass a Turing test of the type that would win the Loebner Silver Prize
criteria.note: GPT-4.5 was judged human 73% of the time in a five-minute three-party test, but the Loebner format ran 25 minutes and required fooling half the judges. The contest has been defunct since 2019.

criteria.label: Score 90% or more on a robust Winograd Schema Challenge such as WinoGrande
criteria.note: Cleared in 2022 by a fine-tuned specialist, ST-MoE-32B at 96.1%. Frontier LLM few-shot scores sit below the bar, with GPT-4 at 87.5%, and leaderboards have stopped reporting it.

criteria.label: Score at the 75th percentile on a full SAT mathematics section, from images of the pages
criteria.note: Assumed rather than shown. GPT-4 reached the 89th percentile on SAT Math, but that evaluation embedded figures into a text prompt. Nobody has published a run from images of the exam pages, which is what the criterion asks for.

criteria.label: Learn Montezuma's Revenge from visual input and explore all 24 rooms in under 100 hours of equivalent play
criteria.note: The rooms stopped being the hard part in 2018; the budget is the bar. The 2026 state of the art uses 400M frames for exploration alone, against roughly 21.6M for 100 hours of play.

criteria.label: Be a single unified system, not sub-systems specialised to each task
criteria.note: No system has been demonstrated on all four tests, let alone one system on all four.

definitions.name: Full AGI: a two-hour adversarial Turing test, and a Ferrari
definitions.quote: Able to reliably pass a 2-hour, adversarial Turing test during which the participants can send text, images, and audio files
definitions.quote_source: Metaculus question 5121. Judges are instructed to ask difficult questions designed to advantage humans and to unmask the computer
definitions.status_today: The two hardest tests here have never been run by anyone. Not failed. Never attempted, in six years. The knowledge tests moved with the field: MMLU is met, APPS at 90% top-1 strict is not, and frontier models are rarely run on APPS any more. The two that need someone to build an apparatus have not moved at all, because nobody has built one. That is a funding gap, not a capability gap. Community estimate November 2032, from 1.9k forecasters.
definitions.flip_condition: Anyone running the two-hour adversarial test. It is the single cheapest unresolved measurement on this page, and its absence is the main reason this question has not moved.
definitions.verification_note: Two of the four sub-criteria have never been attempted by anyone

criteria.label: Pass a 2-hour adversarial Turing test carrying text, images and audio
criteria.note: Never run. The longest published test is five minutes, with a pre-registered fifteen-minute replication, and judges were not adversarial.

criteria.label: Autonomously assemble a 1:8 scale Ferrari 312 T4 model from human-readable instructions
criteria.note: Never attempted. Epoch AI rates comparable household manipulation at tier 2 of 5.

criteria.label: At least 90% mean accuracy across MMLU
criteria.note: Cleared by frontier models.

criteria.label: At least 90% top-1 strict accuracy on APPS interview-level problems
criteria.note: The best published interview-level result, about 80%, comes from a multi-agent plan-code-debug scaffold on a 139-problem subset. Single-shot top-1, which is what the criterion specifies, is around 50%.

criteria.label: Be a single unified system, not sub-systems specialised to each task
criteria.note: Moot while two sub-criteria are unattempted.

definitions.name: The Employment Test: the fraction of jobs machines can do
definitions.quote: To pass the employment test, AI programs must be able to perform the jobs ordinarily performed by humans. Progress toward human-level AI could then be measured by the fraction of these jobs that can be acceptably performed by machines.
definitions.quote_source: Nils J. Nilsson, "Human-Level Artificial Intelligence? Be Serious!", AI Magazine 26(4), 2005
definitions.status_today: Alone among the criteria here, Nilsson did not set a pass mark. He defined progress itself as the fraction of ordinary jobs machines can acceptably perform, which makes this the only entry with a built-in continuous metric rather than a threshold to cross. The closest instrument is the Remote Labor Index, built by CAIS with Scale, which scores whether AI agents can complete real paid freelance projects to the standard a client would accept. The best model reached 15.8% in July 2026, up from 2.5% at launch in October 2025. Set that against GDPval, where the best reported figure is 84.9% wins-or-ties on expert deliverables. Same year, same broad question, and a gap of nearly seventy points. The difference is that GDPval grades a deliverable in isolation while the Remote Labor Index requires the whole job to be finished to a paying client's satisfaction. Nilsson asked for the second.
definitions.flip_condition: The Remote Labor Index crossing 50%, which would be the first time a majority of real remote projects were completed to client standard.
definitions.verification_note: Remote Labor Index is built and scored by CAIS with Scale, independent of the model vendors; the mapping from freelance projects to 'jobs ordinarily performed by humans' is this site's reading
